stem: A pregnant client with preeclampsia develops upper-abdominal pain and laboratory results showing hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and a low platelet count. Which complication is most likely?
rationale: HELLP stands for hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelet count. ACOG notes that it is a serious complication associated with preeclampsia and may include upper-abdominal pain.
educational_objective: Recognize the laboratory triad and clinical context of HELLP syndrome.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
source_document_title: Preeclampsia and High Blood Pressure During Pregnancy FAQ
source_locator: HELLP syndrome: hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelet count; symptoms can include upper-abdominal pain
source_claim_supported: HELLP is defined by hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets and can occur as a severe pregnancy complication.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
correction_summary: Removed unnecessary trimester and nonspecific symptom precision and retained the exact HELLP triad plus supported upper-abdominal pain.
